skill.name: computer-use-agents
skill.description: Build AI agents that interact with computers like humans do - viewing screens, moving cursors, clicking buttons, and typing text. Covers Anthropic's Computer Use, OpenAI's Operator/CUA, and open-source alternatives. Critical focus on sandboxing, security, and handling the unique challenges of vision-based control. Use when: computer use, desktop automation agent, screen control AI, vision-based agent, GUI automation.
skill.summary: Build and evaluate sandboxed computer-use agents for GUI automation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most external command alerts are Markdown fence false positives or constrained Docker setup examples. The meaningful risks are screenshot capture, temporary screenshot files, autonomous GUI control, and broad agent tool exposure, all of which require strong sandboxing and permission controls.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture and temporary image handling
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent, run captures only inside a sandbox, redact sensitive screen areas, and delete temporary screenshots immediately.
Add action allowlists, step limits, visible audit logs, and human confirmation before destructive or credential-related actions.

remediation.issue: Broad bash and text editor tool exposure
remediation.suggestion: Document command allowlists, filesystem scopes, credential isolation, and network egress limits for shell and editor tools.

remediation.issue: Partial documentation snippets may be copied into production
remediation.suggestion: Mark incomplete examples clearly and provide complete safety checks around screenshot, shell, and GUI-control handlers.

content.value_statement: Computer use agents can expose screens, files, and credentials when built without isolation. This skill explains agent loops, sandbox patterns, and tool choices for safer GUI automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains the perception, reasoning, action, and feedback loop for computer-use agents.
Shows Python examples for screenshots, mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.
Outlines Docker and compose patterns for isolated virtual desktop environments.
Covers Anthropic Computer Use tools for computer, bash, and text editor actions.
Highlights security constraints such as network limits, credential isolation, and resource limits.
Notes practical limitations of vision-based UI control and context management.
limitations: Several code examples are partial and should not be copied into production unchanged.
The skill does not provide a complete runnable package or test suite.
Sandbox recommendations still require local security review before deployment.
Model and tool version claims may become outdated as providers update APIs.

use_cases.description: Use the agent loop examples to plan a vision model that observes screens and performs desktop actions.

use_cases.title: Review Sandbox Requirements

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Agent Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the perception, reasoning, action, and feedback loop for a computer-use agent in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Safe Sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sandbox for a desktop automation agent that limits network, filesystem, credentials, and resources.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Agent Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed computer-use agent architecture and identify missing safety controls, monitoring, and human approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Tool Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a hardening checklist for screenshot, mouse, keyboard, bash, and file editing tools in a production computer-use agent.

output_examples.input: Design a sandbox for a desktop automation agent.
output_examples.output: A concise control plan covering isolated virtual display, internal network, scoped temporary storage, non-root execution, resource limits, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Review an agent that can click, type, and run shell commands.
output_examples.output: A risk review that flags sensitive actions, recommends confirmation gates, limits shell commands, and separates test credentials from host credentials.

output_examples.input: Compare full desktop control with browser-only automation.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary covering capability breadth, visual context, attack surface, testing complexity, and when a narrower browser agent is safer.

best_practices: Run computer-use agents only inside isolated environments with no host credential access.
Require human confirmation before payments, account changes, file deletion, or credential entry.
Keep screenshots, action logs, and shell output scoped, redacted, and retained only as needed.
anti_patterns: Do not run a vision-control agent directly on your main desktop.
Do not expose unrestricted bash, editor, or browser access to an untested agent.
Do not store raw screenshots in shared temporary paths without cleanup.

faq.question: What is a computer-use agent?
faq.answer: It is an AI system that observes a screen and uses tools to click, type, scroll, or run commands.

faq.question: Does this skill build a complete agent?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and security guidance for designing and reviewing one.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill discusses Anthropic Computer Use patterns and mentions Claude tool capabilities.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for planning, reviewing, and hardening agent code in Codex and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is exposing screen contents, files, shell commands, or credentials to an autonomous agent.

faq.question: Should I deploy these examples directly?
faq.answer: No. Treat them as design references and add complete sandboxing, logging, cleanup, and approval controls first.
